summary: update_surface_part() test-and-CLEARS the DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A bitmap over the target's page range at :3466-3480, before the gate and regardless of `upload`. mem_dirty has exactly two consumers and both are inside the gate block: `surface->upload_pending |= mem_dirty` on the compatible-hit path (:3747) and `surface->upload_pending = shelf_stale || mem_dirty` on the unshelve path (:3818). With gate_open now `upload && (...)`, a DOWNLOAD call can no longer reach either, so on a binding-less download the dirty bits are consumed and mem_dirty is computed and used by nothing. Before this change that same call opened the gate on the `!current_binding` term and therefore did record the CPU write on the binding it resolved.
scenario: Guest CPU writes the colour surface's VRAM range. A download call for that part runs with the binding absent -- pgraph_vk_surface_update(d, false, ...) from blit.c:446 or blit.c:861, entered because pg->surface_color.draw_dirty is set -- and its test-and-clear at :3475 consumes the dirty bits for the range. The next upload pass finds the binding still absent, opens the gate on !current_binding, and lands on the compatible-hit path at :3747 or the unshelve path at :3818 with mem_dirty now FALSE, because this call's test-and-clear found nothing left. upload_pending stays false, the host image is used, and the guest's write is never uploaded -- verbatim the failure the comment at :3806-3814 says the unshelve mem_dirty test exists to prevent. Amplified by the declined path no longer clearing pg_surface->buffer_dirty: buffer_dirty persists, so the next upload pass unbinds first and, if that part's write is not enabled, the binding is still absent at the following download.
remediation: Make the declined download stop consuming state it cannot use: compute the mem_dirty scan only when `upload`, so the bits survive to the next upload, or carry mem_dirty forward explicitly on the declined branch. Then state in the comment at :3486-3532 what the declined path is allowed to consume -- it currently discusses only the binding. MEDIUM rather than HIGH deliberately: the same loss already happens on a download whose binding is PRESENT (gate closed, mem_dirty discarded), so the class is not new, and the binding-absent case is close to unreachable under master's current policy. It stops being rare in exactly the arm this PR measures, and on master the moment #88's policy re-lands -- which this PR argues it has unblocked.
evidence: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/../vk/surface.c at HEAD d4ca3c7237: :3466-3480 (unconditional bitmap_test_and_clear_atomic), :3538 (new gate), :3545 (if (gate_open)), :3747, :3806-3818, :3873-3909 (download tail); blit.c:446, :861; every occurrence of mem_dirty in update_surface_part read.

summary: dl91_probe's header comment at :309-312 states that the probe is placed after the gate so that "`addr=` is therefore the address that download would have gone to, which is the number worth having". The probe (:329) takes (PGRAPHState const *pg, bool color) -- no address -- and its log line (:349) is "[dl91] frame=%d declined=%lu f_declined=%lu part=%s". There is no addr= field. The call site at :3903 has target.vram_addr in scope, exactly as surf91_overlap_probe's does; surf91_overlap_probe takes hwaddr addr, prints overlap=0x%08 HWADDR_PRIx, and its comment explains at length which address it deliberately does NOT print. The contrast is what makes this an omission rather than a choice.
scenario: dl91_probe is the lane's only instrument for a fix that is a removal, and the prediction's falsifier (5) reads its counter from the arm log rather than from the score. An operator reading that log, told by the code that addr= is the number worth having, greps for it, finds no such field, and either concludes the declines were not address-attributable or re-runs the arm to get it. The counter legs still work; the attribution the comment promises cannot be performed -- and it is the one that would separate "declined a download that would have gone to the wrong address" from "declined a harmless one", which is precisely the limit :298-303 says the counter alone cannot settle.
remediation: Pass target.vram_addr into dl91_probe and print it, matching surf91_overlap_probe, or delete the sentence at :309-312. One parameter either way.
evidence: surface.c at HEAD d4ca3c7237: :296-320 (probe header), :329 (signature), :349 (format string), :3903 (call site, target in scope); :260-289 (surf91_overlap_probe, which does take and print hwaddr addr).

summary: The regenerated shared index is behind master and is the reason the PR cannot fold. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/master HEAD` reports exactly one conflict, CONTENT in docs/testing/nv2a_index.json; GitHub agrees (mergeable: CONFLICTING, mergeStateStatus: DIRTY). Against master's tip the branch copy has provenance.emulator_commit b86517efe7 (this branch's own scaffolding commit) where master has bf0e9b55ba, sites 2833 where master has 2839, and hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/renderer.c locs running BACKWARDS (1096->1071, 1297->1272, 1370->1345) because master's renderer.c has grown 25 lines this branch has not seen. The PR body's "counts are unchanged at 951 symbols / 2833 sites / 103 suites" was true against the base merged on attempt 2 and is not true against master. No suite was dropped: tests_commit 91a0de45ca, suites 103, symbols 951 and gaps 498 all match master.
scenario: The conflict resolved by taking the branch side -- the obvious resolution, since the branch is the side that regenerated the index -- lands an index that drops 6 emulator sites and points every renderer.c gap 25 lines off. The index is what briefs and the gap tooling resolve `loc` from, so the next lane sent to a renderer.c line arrives at the wrong one, and a gap master currently tracks stops being tracked with nothing saying it was dropped. Taking master's side instead silently discards this branch's surface.c locs, which are the ones the change actually moved. Either way the PR is unfoldable until someone resolves it.
remediation: Merge origin/master, regenerate the index on the merged tree with the same tests_root/tests_commit (91a0de45ca..., which is what master carries), and confirm sites >= 2839 and suites == 103 before committing. Re-verify afterwards that aec524681e and 7980d1caa2 are still ancestors and say so rather than assume it. Do not rebase -- the prediction names both refs.
evidence: git merge-tree --write-tree origin/master HEAD (CONFLICT content, docs/testing/nv2a_index.json); gh pr view 148 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus -> CONFLICTING/DIRTY; json.load of both copies: provenance {emulator_commit bf0e9b55ba vs b86517efe7, sites 2839 vs 2833, suites 103 vs 103, symbols 951 vs 951, gaps 498 vs 498, tests_commit 91a0de45ca both}; git diff origin/master HEAD -- docs/testing/nv2a_index.json.

summary: :178-181 now reads "REMOVE ALL FOUR -- surf92_probe, surf91_overlap_probe and dl91_probe here, clr89_probe/clr91_probe in vk/draw.c", which is five names. dl91_probe's own lifetime line at :319 says "with the other four", i.e. five in total, which is the correct count and contradicts the heading four lines of diff away. The pre-existing text said "REMOVE ALL THREE" over four names, so the off-by-one is inherited rather than introduced; the diff touched that exact line, incremented the wrong number, and added an internal contradiction that was not there before. The block's stated purpose is that "the set still leaves together".
scenario: Whoever closes #91 removes probes by the count the heading gives, removes four, and ships the fifth -- an always-on SURF92_LOG (__android_log_print on Android, fprintf(stderr) elsewhere, :193-200) on a per-draw surface path, in a release build, with nothing left in the tree saying it should have gone.
remediation: Make it five, or drop the numeral and let the list be the list.
evidence: surface.c at HEAD d4ca3c7237: :170-186 (lifetime block), :319 (dl91_probe LIFETIME line), :193-200 (SURF92_LOG); git diff origin/master...HEAD shows the THREE -> FOUR edit.
